mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP engine typically costs £1,800-£3,100 supply-only, depending on supplier and condition. Used units start from £700. Reconditioned units range £1,500-£2,400. Supply & fit adds £400-£800 labour. Main dealer replacement can exceed £6,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP (EP6FDT) engine problems are timing chain stretch and tensioner failure causing cold-start rattle, carbon buildup on intake valves from direct injection, high-pressure fuel pump failure causing hard starting, and turbocharger oil feed line leaks.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound and the replacement cost stays below the vehicle's value. With 2008 1.6 THP values typically £4,000-£14,000, a rebuilt engine at £1,800-£3,100 represents a significant investment. For sub-£5,000 examples, a used engine from £700 may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP (EP6FDT) engine can reach 120,000-150,000 miles. However, timing chain issues can appear as early as 40,000 miles. Regular oil changes with correct PSA-approved oil, timely timing chain replacement and carbon cleaning are essential for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP and 1.2 PureTech engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.6 THP (EP6FDT) is a 1.6-litre turbocharged four-cylinder producing 165hp, while the 1.2 PureTech is a 1.2-litre turbocharged three-cylinder producing 82-130hp. The 1.6 THP uses a timing chain (which can stretch), while the PureTech uses a wet timing belt (which can degrade). The 1.6 THP is more powerful but also more complex and less reliable.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP engine code is EP6FDT (5GZ) or EP6CDT for earlier variants. It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP was the most powerful petrol engine offered in the first-generation (A94) 2008, delivering performance that set it apart from the more common PureTech three-cylinder units. Part of the BMW-Peugeot joint-developed Prince engine family, the 1.6 THP (EP6) featured twin-scroll turbocharging and direct injection, producing up to 165hp. However, its complexity and well-documented reliability issues - particularly timing chain stretch and carbon buildup - have made it a growing source of replacement enquiries. The 1.6 THP was available in limited UK volumes, primarily in higher-spec GT and GTi-badged variants from 2016 onwards.

milestones.description: **2016** - 1.6 THP introduced to Peugeot 2008 range with 165hp (121kW) output
**2017** - EP6FDT engine code (5GZ) becomes the primary THP variant for 2008
**2018** - Timing chain and tensioner revisions introduced to address early failures
**2019** - First-generation 2008 production ends; 1.6 THP discontinued in favour of PureTech turbo units

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every EP6FDT engine fitted to the Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP (EP6FDT) delivers strong performance, but its Prince engine architecture - jointly developed with BMW - has well-documented weaknesses. Timing chain stretch, carbon buildup and turbocharger issues are the primary drivers of replacement enquiries. Unlike the PureTech engines, the 1.6 THP uses a timing chain rather than a wet belt, but chain tensioner failure remains a significant concern. Every rebuilt Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded timing components and refreshed ancillary systems, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP Engines Rattle and Lose Timing
problems.rootCause: The Prince engine's timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack to develop. Over time, the chain stretches and the plastic guides wear, leading to rattling on cold start and, in severe cases, chain jump and valve-piston contact. The issue is so widespread that Peugeot released a TSB with revised tensioner and guide parts.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of chain, tensioner (revised), guides and VANOS sprockets with updated parts
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components, new turbo seals and HPFP, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped or caused valve damage

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP exhibits the characteristic cold-start rattle, address it immediately. A timing chain kit replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Once the rattle is constant or accompanied by loss of power, the chain has likely jumped - at that stage, a rebuilt EP6FDT engine with upgraded timing components is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EP6FDT Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP engine prices

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup - Why Direct Injection Causes Power Loss and Rough Idle
problems.rootCause: Direct injection petrol engines do not wash the intake valves with fuel, allowing carbon deposits from the PCV system to accumulate on valve stems and seats. This restricts airflow, causing rough idle, hesitation, reduced power and increased fuel consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media blasting of intake valves to remove carbon deposits
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before valve damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with refreshed valvetrain and intake system
repairOptions.longevity: Only necessary if carbon buildup has caused valve or piston damage

problems.recommendation: Carbon buildup is a known characteristic of direct injection engines. A professional walnut blast cleaning every 40,000-60,000 miles is a worthwhile preventative measure. If the engine has been running poorly for an extended period, carbon scoring may have damaged cylinder walls - in which case a rebuilt unit is the only reliable fix.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP engine prices

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump & Turbocharger Failure - Additional Vulnerabilities
problems.rootCause: The high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) can wear internally, causing hard starting and loss of power. The turbocharger's oil feed line can leak, starving the turbo of lubrication and leading to bearing failure. Both issues are well-documented on the Prince engine family.

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - HPFP & Turbo Oil Feed Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of high-pressure fuel pump and turbo oil feed lines
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before turbo damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new HPFP, turbo and oil feed system
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 2008 1.6 THP has hard starting or turbo lag, have the HPFP and oil feed lines inspected immediately. Replacing these components early can prevent catastrophic turbo failure. Once turbo debris has contaminated the oil system, a full rebuilt engine is the safest option.
